title: Points, Ticks & P&L
hook: MNQ = $2 per point. MGC = $10 per point. Know your numbers before you trade.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to calculate a trade's dollar P&L from points, point value, and contract count.

blocks.heading: Points and ticks are how the market moves. P&L is what that movement means to you.

beats.heading: Two units of movement
beats.body: Points are larger units of movement. Ticks are smaller pieces inside those points.

beats.heading: Where it becomes real money
beats.body: P&L is the money attached to that movement once you add your instrument and contract count. This is where it stops being chart language and starts being real.

blocks.heading: Watch P&L scale with contract size
blocks.prompt: MNQ moves 30 points at $2/point. Tap a contract size to see the dollar result.

blocks.heading: Build the P&L formula
blocks.prompt: Tap the three pieces in the order you'd calculate them.

items.label: × point value
items.desc: What that instrument pays per point

blocks.successFeedback: That's the formula — points × point value × contracts.
blocks.failFeedback: Close — the order is points moved, then point value, then contract count.

blocks.quote: Bigger size makes the same move louder — the chart may be normal while your emotions are not. Staying small enough to stay teachable matters.

questions.question: If 1 point = 4 ticks, how many ticks are in 2 points?
A trader says "I made 30 points today" without mentioning contracts or instrument. Why is that statement incomplete?
options: Points alone don't tell you the dollar result — you also need the point value and contract count
It's a complete statement — points are all that matter
Points and dollars are always the same number
questions.why: 30 points on MNQ at 1 contract is a very different dollar outcome than 30 points on MGC at 5 contracts.

takeaways: Points are big units of movement, ticks are the smaller pieces inside them.
P&L = points moved × point value × contract count.
Bigger size makes the same chart move feel louder emotionally.
remember: The chart may be normal while your emotions are not — size is why.
